chunks: What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a man who wraps himself in a single garment during his salat (prayer). He said: "He should not wrap himself in a single garment; but as for wearing it across himself so that he covers his shoulders, there is no harm."
Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is disliked for a person to perform salat (prayer) wearing a turban that has no under-chin wrap.

key_terms.بِثَوْبٍ وَاحِدٍ: with a single garment, referring to the mode of dress in prayer
key_terms.حَنَكَ: the under-chin wrap of a turban
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being discussed
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm, indicating permissibility
key_terms.مَنْكِبَيْهِ: his two shoulders, whose covering is mentioned as acceptable
key_terms.يَتَوَشَّحَ: to wear a garment across oneself, in a way that covers properly
key_terms.يَشْتَمِلُ: to wrap oneself up, referring here to an improper style of covering oneself
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: it is disliked, indicating karahah rather than prohibition

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying while wrapped in a single garment or wearing a turban without a chin-wrap?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning proper dress in salat (prayer). It forbids wrapping oneself in a single garment in a manner that is improper, while permitting wearing it in a way that covers the shoulders; it also adds that praying in a turban without a chin-wrap is disliked.
